channel.title: New Straits Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from New Straits Times (nst.com.my)

item.title: RHB Research upgrades Bursa Malaysia to 'Buy'
item.description: KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Research has upgraded its rating on Bursa Malaysia Bhd to “Buy” from “Neutral”, citing expectations that the exchange will benefit from improving liquidity inflows.

item.title: Tapir killed while crossing back to the forest
item.description: DUNGUN: A male tapir was killed after being struck by a car at Km8 of Jalan Bandar Al-Mukhtafi Billah Shah–Paka near Kampung Santong here last night.

item.title: IGP: Police finalising probe into ex-FMT journalist over forum question
item.description: KUALA LUMPUR: The investigation paper involving a former Free Malaysia Today (FMT) journalist, following a controversial question he posed during a public forum last month, will be submitted to the Attorney-General’s Chambers (A-GC) soon.

item.title: Self-funded Maba emerges as exemplary model for national sports bodies
item.description: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Basketball Association (Maba) has achieved financial independence through a property redevelopment project, removing its reliance on government funding.

item.title: We should have 100,000 public EV chargers by 2030 - and let the people "vote" where they go
item.description: THEY say it is a chicken-and-egg problem: which should come first, the electric vehicle or the charger?

item.title: Auto sector's OMV issue resolved, for now
item.description: THE long-running issue over the revised open market value (OMV) excise duty calculation - the so-called 402 regulations - has been resolved, for now.

item.title: Nine Kelantan petrol stations under scrutiny for suspiciously high sales
item.description: RANTAU PANJANG: Nine petrol stations along the Kelantan border have come under scrutiny for recording unusually high sales volumes, prompting suspicions of unlawful activity involving petrol and diesel.

item.title: Police deploy 1,400 personnel as 1.5 million expected at Batu Caves for Thaipusam
item.description: KUALA LUMPUR: An estimated 1.5 million visitors are expected to throng Batu Caves throughout the Thaipusam celebration this year, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain said.

item.title: Precision engineering firms gain traction in auto sector
item.description: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia’s automotive manufacturing sector is seeing greater participation from local precision engineering firms as production shifts toward higher-value and technology-driven activities.

item.title: Thaipusam transforms Penang streets with colour, devotion
item.description: GEORGE TOWN: Thaipusam devotion begins long before sunrise in Penang, as faith takes to the streets.
